description_full: Meitu, Inc., an investment holding company, engages in the development and provision of products that streamline the production of photo, video, and design with other AI-powered products in Mainland China and internationally. Its product portfolio includes Meitu app, Wink, DesignKit, BeautyCam, Kaipai, WHEE, and MOKI; ecosystem products, such as ZCOOL, RoboNeo, and MiracleVision. In addition, it is involved in the provision of online advertising and other IVAS by offering a portfolio of photo and community apps, as well as information technology services; smart hardware business; and solutions for beauty industry. Meitu, Inc. was founded in 2008 and is headquartered in Xiamen, the People's Republic of China.
ceo_bio: Mr. Zeyuan  Wu | Founder, Executive Chairman & CEO | Age 44 | Compensation: $772,813 (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $293K ranks in the bottom quartile among Communication Services peers. Each employee generates $92K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $9K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 3× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (9/10). R&D investment of 24% of revenue (heavy) signals commitment to product development and talent. Note: heavy R&D investment has not yet translated to above-average workforce productivity — watch for commercialisation lag.
financial_summary: MEITU INC is a mid-cap communication services business with a $2.4B market cap on $579M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +20% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +6.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 67% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $181M in free cash flow — roughly 31 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 28% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
